What to look for
FSI Workflows and Agents
Limited FSI-specific agent depth; mostly horizontal, pilot-stage or heavily customized; little production proof.
Multiple relevant workflows and some production evidence, but maturity or packaging is uneven.
Broad mature FSI agent/workflow portfolio with repeatable, packaged and production-scaled examples.
FSI specificity, breadth, production maturity and customer adoption.
Priority Use Cases
Few clearly prioritized sub-industry use cases with limited adoption or investment evidence.
Several priority use cases with credible demand and some adoption, but coverage is uneven.
Broad set of high-value use cases with clear investment, GTM focus, demand and production proof.
Investment focus, customer demand, adoption, measurable outcomes and breadth.
Data Ecosystem and Connectors
Few specialist FSI data/system connectors; mostly horizontal access and significant custom integration.
Good financial-data and enterprise connectivity, but important sub-industry or plug-and-play gaps remain.
Deep specialist financial-data/system ecosystem embedded into agents and workflows with broad usable coverage.
Breadth, specialist depth, systems-of-record coverage, ease of use and workflow integration.
Compliance, Governance, Security and Trust
Mostly generic controls with material FSI gaps in residency, governance, explainability, auditability or agent control.
Strong enterprise foundation with FSI applicability, but some controls remain horizontal, newer or incomplete.
Comprehensive regulated-FSI controls with mature governance, privacy, residency, auditability and agent oversight.
FSI specificity, maturity, regulatory coverage, evidence and production use.
Partner Ecosystem
Limited FSI-specialist network or production delivery capacity; high reliance on generalists.
Established GSIs/ISVs/FSI specialists, but depth, certifications or implementation capability is uneven.
Broad mature ecosystem with strong FSI specialists, co-build, certifications, implementation and GTM scale.
Breadth, FSI specialization, delivery capability, co-build, certification and reach.
Marketplace
Limited relevant FSI catalog or little evidence of material procurement/transactions.
Meaningful FSI catalog and some commercial activity, but depth or scale is uneven.
Large specialist catalog with strong procurement, transaction and ecosystem scale.
Catalog breadth, FSI depth, commercial activity and procurement/deployment value.
GTM Execution
Mostly horizontal GTM with limited dedicated FSI messaging, teams, events or enablement.
Visible FSI GTM and customer engagement, but inconsistent by sub-industry/channel.
Coordinated FSI GTM with dedicated teams, events, executive engagement, content, partners and customer proof.
FSI specificity, channel breadth, executive reach, enablement and repeatability.
Customer References and Proof Points
Few named production references, limited scale and few measurable outcomes.
Multiple credible references but evidence of scale/outcomes is uneven.
Extensive named production proof across workflows with strong scale and quantified outcomes.
Number, relevance, production scale, sub-industry breadth and measurable outcomes.
Industry Solutions and FSI Verticalization
Predominantly horizontal; relies heavily on customer/partner customization.
Some packaged FSI products/workflows but vertical depth is concentrated.
Deep first-party verticalization with dedicated sub-industry products and persona-specific workflows.
First-party IP, sub-industry specificity, packaging, breadth and reduced customization.
Customer Objections
Significant unresolved barriers materially hinder adoption (cost, integration, security, maturity, etc.).
Important objections remain but have credible mitigations; some still slow production.
Major objections are well mitigated and have limited impact on scaled adoption.
For this parameter only: High = fewer/better-mitigated barriers; Low = more material unresolved barriers.
